title: fix(ui): keep automation history with its selected task
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: switching automations can show the previous task's runs under the newly selected task, and a successful run-history retry can leave the old failure banner visible.

## User Impact

History stays attached to the selected automation and filters. Refreshing the same history retains its last results while loading; a successful retry clears its own error while preserving feedback from other actions. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request ownership already rejected late responses, but retained rows had no lasting query identity and history failures shared the action error field. The history owner now uses the same query comparison for retained history and active requests, and owns history errors separately from action/status feedback. Pagination and coalesced refreshes keep their existing request authority.

## Evidence

Both production-browser regressions fail on original code and pass with the fix: select a second automation while its history request is held and then fails; recover from an initial history error with explicit Refresh. Two owner-level regressions also fail on the original retained-row assertion. All 308 focused controller, refresh, page, and view tests pass, including same-query retention, changed-query retirement, stale completions, pagination, and preserving action feedback with identical error text.

Independent Codex P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. The full changed-file gate passes, including core test and UI type graphs, formatting, i18n, guards, all three unused-export scans, typed lint, and stylelint. The earlier hosted run failed in an unchanged desktop-resize real-Gateway test; that failure is retained in [run 35082052137](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35082052137). This branch now incorporates the independently landed desktop fixture readiness repair #149975. The next hosted run exposed the pre-existing private-completion fixture race ([run 35088368606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35088368606)). Main now fixes that fixture in #149124 by running and joining a real child before the unchanged settlement assertion. This branch incorporates that canonical repair. With matching frozen dependencies and updated browser helpers, both Cron browser regressions pass again; formatting, diff checks, frozen hashes, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. All six feature files are unchanged. Unmodified current main separately passes the original 35-file/124-test Gateway group. The next hosted run exposed the new line-cap gate in the existing oversized controller. History loading, pagination, request retirement, and retained-query state now live together in a dedicated history module; all callers migrate directly, and the seven moved function bodies retain their behavior. Fresh proof passes all 308 focused tests, both production-browser regressions, UI and affected test type graphs, typed lint, all three unused-export scans, formatting, and the canonical line-cap gate. Independent review found no actionable findings; the complete extraction and callers were also reviewed together. That hosted run additionally timed out in an unchanged queued-edit browser flow; its cause remains unresolved. One local replay of all ten original ordered cases passes on Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.3.4, with unchanged assertions and timeouts. A later CI failure repeated on an unrelated Incognito branch; that job actually executes Node 24.20.0 and runs this file after 41 bundled browser files, so the single-file local pass does not reproduce its full environment. This does not establish a Cron cause or a fix for that timeout. The first extraction passed the runtime-cycle checker but exposed a type-only cycle in Madge. Shared automation types now live in a leaf contract consumed directly by the controller, history owner, and all UI callers. Both cycle checks report zero; the repeated 308 tests, affected type graphs, lint, line-cap, and export scans pass, with fresh independent review. [Fresh exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35095634835). A full 230-case replay passed all ten queued-edit cases; a separate controlled route-order reproduction now demonstrates that leaving Chat can cancel an intercepted Review edit navigation. That separate owner repair is underway; this PR does not claim to fix its historical CI timeout. Browser captures use synthetic data and a mocked Gateway, not a live provider.

### Selecting a different automation

Before, Beta displays Alpha's run after Beta's history request fails. After, Beta shows its own failure without another task's rows.

![Before: Beta displays another automation’s run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0313402-a475-41d1-8446-f58846bf3748)

![After: Beta history excludes Alpha’s runs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18e5eeb2-6e97-402b-97ec-aeefef4fc35c)

### Recovering history

Before, a successful retry shows the recovered run alongside the obsolete error. After, the recovered run is visible and the history error is cleared.

![Before: successful history retry leaves the old error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8cbaa147-693a-4b00-87d1-31a915a4d83d)

![After: successful retry clears the history error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d43236a-1382-47d7-bded-6b6a14c5df8e)
